problem.statement: Input exactly two whitespace-separated integers a,b, -100<=a,b<=100. Output a+b as one integer.
Input n (1<=n<=8), followed by exactly n integers a[i] (-9<=a[i]<=9). Output the maximum sum over all NONEMPTY contiguous intervals. No test-count header.

Input n and W (1<=n<=8,1<=W<=20), followed by n pairs weight,value (1<=weight<=10,1<=value<=20). Each item can be selected at most once. Output maximum total value of a subset with total weight<=W; empty subset allowed. No test-count header.
Input n (1<=n<=8), followed by exactly n integers a[i] (0<=a[i]<=5). Output the number of distinct values in the array. The input array is not guaranteed to be sorted. No test-count header.

Input t test cases (1<=t<=5000). Each case has n (1<=n<=5000) and three arrays a,b,c of length n, with each entry between 1 and 3*n; sum n across cases<=5000. Count ordered triples of cyclic starting positions i,j,k in [0,n-1] such that a[(i+r)%n]<b[(j+r)%n]<c[(k+r)%n] for EVERY r=0..n-1. Output one integer per case. Brute force should enumerate triples on tiny generated n, while still accepting the full sample.
